nodes.description: AAV delivery of functional L- or M-opsin is investigational. Mouse studies restore partial cone ERG responses and outer-segment structure, with age and model background affecting rescue. The 2025 comparison of DKO and C198R/Opn1sw-null mice found no significant genotype difference in therapeutic windows, and weaker responses in older animals. All-cone models also respond after treatment at five months. These studies do not establish a human age cutoff or efficacy. Intravitreal ADVM-062 produced new long-wavelength responses in gerbils and foveal transduction in nonhuman primates; mild ocular inflammation occurred at higher doses. Neither species was a human BCM treatment cohort.

nodes.description: Regulatory loss, coding deletion, splice defects and inactivating coding variants converge on reduced or absent functional L/M photopigment. Cys203Arg can cause misfolding and reduced opsin abundance; in mouse retina its equivalent C198R protein is undetectable or greatly reduced without the aggregates seen in transfected cells. Met273Lys recombinant opsin lacks normal absorption after reconstitution with retinal. The effects of different coding alleles should not be assumed to share a single toxic-aggregation mechanism.

Reduced opsin disrupts outer-segment formation and maintenance. Patients have variable outer-retinal and ellipsoid-zone abnormalities. Mouse opsin-deficiency models have shortened or absent outer segments and reduced localization of phototransduction proteins; early gene augmentation can partially restore these structures. Human adaptive-optics imaging reveals non-waveguiding cells, but their spectral identity, functional competence and capacity for rescue are not established by morphology alone.

nodes.description: Specific combinations of common exon 3 variants cause exon skipping. LIAVA minigenes show essentially complete loss of correctly spliced product, while LIVVA and other haplotypes retain variable amounts. Exon 3 skipping changes the reading frame and introduces a premature stop; nonsense-mediated decay is a proposed consequence. Assays using cDNA distinguish splicing from protein effects: LIAVA protein remains functional in mice, whereas LVAVA has additional protein-level defects in an overlapping cone dystrophy spectrum. Clinical severity depends on the other expressed opsin copies and promoter context.

nodes.description: Deletion of the upstream LCR removes an enhancer required for expression of the adjacent L/M opsin genes. LCR-only deletions can silence otherwise retained coding genes, whereas many larger deletions also remove part or all of those genes. Transgenic studies support competition between opsin promoters for LCR interaction. A 358-bp critical interval was inferred by patient deletion mapping, not established as an isolated minimal enhancer by a functional deletion assay.

nodes.description: Pathogenic array configurations abolish or markedly reduce functional L- and M-opsin expression. They include LCR-only deletions, larger deletions removing regulatory and coding sequence, coding variants in a single residual or hybrid gene or in multiple expressed genes, and splice-disrupting exon 3 haplotypes. Cys203Arg is recurrent; Arg247Ter, Pro307Leu and functionally tested Met273Lys are additional examples. Array collapse followed by point mutation is one route, not a requirement for all BCM genotypes.

nodes.description: Retinal imaging and some clinical family studies support progressive macular damage in a subset. A 2018 retrospective series compared 21 deletion and 13 Cys203Arg cases and found greater preservation of foveal structure in the latter group. Cross-sectional age associations must be distinguished from longitudinal change. In a 2024 cohort, seven patients had serial OCT over a median 6.5 years with variable structural changes; quantitative outer nuclear layer thickness showed no change, and the two patients with repeated adaptive-optics images had stable mosaics. Progression is neither absent in all BCM nor uniform across patients.
